note: Rebuilt 2026-09-02 against v1.0.1 (decklist_sha256 7ce22fd6...) after the bloodline branch merged 12 swaps. The previous model was written against v1.0.0 and named 12 cards that are no longer in the 99. Every card name here was checked against deck-facts; every figure is quoted from `engine-facts`/`deck-audit` rather than computed.
thesis: Edgar mints a free Vampire on every Vampire cast and three replacement doublers turn one mint into eight - but v1.0.1 stopped asking those bodies to connect and started asking them to DIE: nine cards convert them into cards, counters and life loss at every seat, and the two checker-passed kill routes are a doubled attack drain and a two-card lifegain loop, neither of which needs combat damage to land.

stages.label: THIRTY-EIGHT SOURCES FOR A DECK THAT CASTS FOUR SPELLS A TURN
stages.what_it_does: Thirty-two lands plus five rocks, and one body that turns into mana. The declared ramp component (Sol Ring, Arcane Signet, Talisman of Indulgence, Herald's Horn, Patchwork Banner) is drawn in 67.0% of games, mean turn 3.54, and deck-audit still reads the axis UNDER at 8 copies against a 10-12 target while colour-sources sits 4 short in the worst colour. That shortfall has one address: Bloodletter of Aclazotz is the ONLY cost in the 99 with three or more identical coloured pips ({1}{B}{B}{B}) - enumerated over every mana cost in cards.json - and it is half the deck's fastest verified kill. Master of Dark Rites files here rather than with the sacrifice outlets because its output is mana, but deck-facts flags the catch: its {B}{B}{B} is spend-only-on-Vampire-Cleric-Demon SPELLS, and an activated ability is not a spell, so it accelerates toward a commander without paying for what the commander then does. Bloodletter is a Vampire Demon, so it qualifies twice over. One land is also an engine piece: Midgar, City of Mako's Adventure half, Reactor Raid, sacrifices a creature to draw two.
cards: Midgar, City of Mako // Reactor Raid

stages.label: CAST A CHEAP VAMPIRE AND A BODY APPEARS - THE ONLY THING THAT HAS TO HAPPEN FIRST
stages.what_it_does: Nothing in this deck happens until a Vampire spell is CAST. Edgar's eminence fires from the command zone - checker-passed twice, in stacks 002 and 010, which read the intervening-'if' again on resolution and confirm the ability functions from the zone it names - so the ignition half the pilot owns is free and undrawable in 100% of games. The half that must be found is the spell: a castable Vampire is drawn in 95.1% of games at mean turn 2.19, the healthiest figure in the brief, and it is the leg every checker-passed kill proof opens on. The six cards beside Edgar are the members whose contribution is dominated by being that spell - four are printed keywords and nothing else, Knight of the Ebon Legion adds a pump activation and Voldaren Epicure an entry ping plus a Blood token - so they can be cast alongside the plan rather than instead of it. Nighthawk Scavenger is the same card at {1}{B}{B} and sits above the declaration's mana-value-2 line. Voldaren Epicure adds one damage to each opponent and a Blood token on the way past. The point of the stage is not that these bodies are good; it is that casting one of them is what turns Edgar on, and everything downstream is priced off that 95.1%.

stages.label: THE BODIES ARE THE RESOURCE, AND THREE CARDS DECIDE HOW MANY THERE ARE
stages.what_it_does: The thing this engine converts is 1/1 Vampire tokens, and the deck holds no card that IS one - so the stage's members are the cards that decide the count. Three replacement doublers stack multiplicatively on the single eminence event: stack 002 records Anointed Procession + Mondrak taking one token to four (1->2->4), and stack 010 records all three taking it to eight (1->2->4->8), order-independent because each doubler gets exactly one opportunity at the event and any modified event replacing it. The declared multiplier component is drawn in 67.3% of games, mean turn 3.61. Five of these seven also make bodies without Edgar - Bloodline Keeper taps for a 2/2 flier, Mavren Fein mints on every nontoken Vampire attack, Charismatic Conqueror taxes opponents' untapped entries, Elspeth's +1 makes a Soldier, and Legion's Landing arrives as a token and flips into a land that makes more. Read the 400-game Forge result before pricing this stage as a win: on a go-wide refactor, combat damage to players fell 29.07 to 18.20 because 1/1 tokens do not connect. Eight tokens is not eight damage. It is eight things to convert.

stages.label: THE THING v1.0.1 WAS BUILT TO FIX
stages.what_it_does: Four logged games say the same thing: the deck ran out of steam on card draw. This stage is the answer bloodline bought. Ten of the eleven are draw; the declared component is nine cards and reads 84.1% assembled, mean turn 2.68, second only to the castable-Vampire leg among the eleven declared components - and yet deck-audit still reads card-advantage UNDER at 7 copies against a 10 target, because the taxonomy cannot see Bloodtracker, Champion of Dusk, Preacher of the Schism, Castle Locthwain, Minas Tirith or Midgar's Adventure half, among others it names. Five of these turn a body LEAVING THE BATTLEFIELD into cards rather than reading off casts - Crossway Troublemakers (2 life per Vampire death), Liliana (every creature death), Skullclamp (two cards per equipped body), Bloodtracker (a card per counter when it leaves), and High-Society Hunter, whose clause is 'another NONTOKEN creature' and therefore never sees an eminence token. That is the shape the pilot's 2026-09-01 game demonstrated: an opponent's Goblin Sharpshooter pinging the token board fed the draw rather than emptying it. Vampiric Tutor is the eleventh, and it is not card advantage - it is the reason a 4.2% component reads 9.6% assisted and a 7.6% one reads 14.6%.

stages.label: NINE OUTLETS, AND THE ONE THAT MAKES THEM PAY
stages.what_it_does: This is the component bloodline actually added, and until 2026-09-01 nothing in the declaration described it - the goldfish's sacrifice cap only started firing (0.0 -> 0.003) once the target existed. Seven of these are free outlets: no mana, no tap, sacrifice a creature and get something. Drawn in 77.6% of games, mean turn 3.04. They are the machine that turns a stage of disposable bodies into cards (Skullclamp, Crossway Troublemakers), drain (Blood Artist, Cruel Celebrant), mana (Ashnod's Altar), and counters. Cordial Vampire files here rather than with the lords because it is the piece that answers the 400-game finding: every death puts a +1/+1 counter on EACH Vampire, which is how a board of 1/1s that cannot connect becomes a board of 2/2s and 3/3s that can. Stack 002 is explicit that it never triggers on a board where nothing dies - the mint alone is not the engine, the mint plus an outlet is. One warning that is about the bench and not the deck: Forge's evaluator will not pay a cost it cannot price, and Ashnod's Altar activated 0 times in 59 castings under both AI profiles - a bench measurement on a sacrifice deck, not one taken on this list. A Forge figure on this stage is a floor, not a measurement.

stages.label: EVERY SEAT, EVERY TURN, WITHOUT AN ATTACK CONNECTING
stages.what_it_does: What the converted bodies actually buy. Two death drains bill on every creature that dies - Blood Artist one target player, Cruel Celebrant EACH opponent, a difference of three-to-one in a pod and the reason they are not interchangeable; the pair is drawn in 37.2% of games and is a two-card component, the thinnest declared here apart from the two one-card kill pieces. Two lifegain converters turn the deck's heavy lifelink into life loss: Vito and Sanguine Bond share the same trigger word for word. Five lords and counter-payoffs raise what a body is worth in combat - a lord or anthem is drawn in 80.2% of games, mean turn 3.14 - and five removal spells answer what the drain cannot. deck-audit reads interaction OVER at 12 copies against a 5-6 target and interaction-breadth UNDER at 4 classes, with land the class it detects no answer for; that is an oracle-text heuristic and a floor, not a verdict. The stage's job is that none of it needs combat damage to land, which is exactly what the 400-game run said this deck could not rely on.

stages.label: FIVE CARDS HELD, AND FOUR OF THEM ARE FREE OR NEARLY
stages.what_it_does: Held, not cast. Deflecting Swat and Flawless Maneuver cost nothing while a commander is on the board or in the zone, and Edgar is in one of those places in every game; Boros Charm is two mana for indestructible on EVERY permanent you control and Teferi's Protection phases the whole board out - reading all five, those are the two that reach the enchantment doublers, since Flawless Maneuver and Akroma's Will name creatures only. Teferi's is also the answer to a sweeper this deck has no other reply to: deck-audit reads sweepers at 0 copies. Akroma's Will is the exception: with a commander it is both modes, which is a kill spell as often as it is insurance. The component is drawn in 68.3% of games, mean turn 3.55, and deck-audit reads protection OVER at 8 copies against a 5-7 target, counting self-protecting bodies like Mondrak and Yahenni that are filed in other stages here.

stages.label: TWO CHECKER-PASSED ROUTES, AND BOTH REST ON ONE CARD EACH
stages.what_it_does: Route one is combat-adjacent and does not need damage to land. Stack 003: seven attacking Vampires give seven Sanctum Seeker triggers; Bloodletter doubles each opponent's loss independently because it is your turn, so each seat loses 14, and the opponent at 14 is eliminated by state-based actions BEFORE blockers are declared. Your own lifegain is not doubled - Bloodletter replaces only opponents' loss. Route two is the infinite: Bloodthirsty Conqueror with Vito (stack 004) or Sanguine Bond (stack 006), both checker-passed as deterministic, shortcut-legal, zero-additional-mana table kills. The honest part is the price. Both routes are single points of failure that deck-audit has already priced: Bloodletter is 7.1% of opening sevens and 4.2% assembled (9.6% with the tutor), Conqueror 7.1% and 7.6% assembled (14.6% assisted). The Haunt of Hightower sits here as the combat close - a 4/4 flying lifelink that grows on every card entering an opponent's graveyard - and it is a six-mana body, not a plan. Two one-card lines and a fatty is a ceiling, and stating it is not the same as calling it a defect.

The same loop with the enchantment half - Bond's trigger is word-for-word Vito's. Two contained lines, one shared body: this is why Conqueror is a priced single point of failure rather than redundancy.

READING (no stack). Bloodletter is the only cost in the 99 with three identical coloured pips ({1}{B}{B}{B}), enumerated over every mana cost in cards.json, and Master of Dark Rites adds exactly {B}{B}{B} spendable on Vampire, Cleric and Demon SPELLS - Bloodletter is a Vampire Demon. Sweeping every 'Add' clause in the 99, it is the only source that produces three mana at once (Nomad Outpost and Savai Triome add one of three colours, not three), and it charges a body to do it.

READING (no stack). The doubled tokens are what the free outlets eat; the multiplier component is drawn 67.3% and the outlet component 77.6%, but NOTHING in the declaration measures the pair, which is the whole of bloodline's engine. See proposed_goldfish_edits.

READING (no stack). Sacrifice a token, draw a card: Crossway Troublemakers pays 2 life per Vampire death, Skullclamp two cards per equipped body. This is the loop the pilot's 2026-09-01 game ran when an opponent's pinger fed the draw instead of emptying the board. High-Society Hunter does NOT see this - its clause is 'another nontoken creature'.

READING (no stack). Each converted body bills the table on the way out. The asymmetry matters and is not interchangeable: Blood Artist drains one target player, Cruel Celebrant each opponent - three-to-one in a pod - and the pair is a two-card component at 37.2%.

READING (no stack). The answer to the 400-game finding. Every death puts a +1/+1 counter on each Vampire; the lords add a static +1/+1 each. A 1/1 that does not connect becomes a 3/3 that does, and the deck buys that with deaths rather than with more tokens.

READING (no stack). Token entries draw cards - but read the caps before pricing it: both abilities say 'This ability triggers only once each turn', so eight tokens from stack 010's board draw two cards, not sixteen.
READING (no stack). The single tutor is the whole difference between the unassisted and assisted figures on both one-card routes: Conqueror 7.6% -> 14.6%, Bloodletter 4.2% -> 9.6% (deck-audit).

READING (no stack). The doublers are enchantments and a legend, so the creature-only insurance does not cover them: of the five protection cards only Teferi's Protection (phases out all permanents) and Boros Charm (indestructible on every permanent) reach Anointed Procession and Mondrak. Mondrak's own indestructible counter costs two other permanents.

READING (no stack). Ignition is priced in mana, not in cards: a castable Vampire is drawn in 95.1% of games at mean turn 2.19, so the binding constraint on how many eminence triggers a turn buys is how many spells the mana casts. Herald's Horn cuts each by {1} and digs for the next.

map_disagreements.component: A castable Vampire drawn - the eminence trigger every kill proof opens on
map_disagreements.why: The single most scattered component in the brief - 13 cards, 4 cities - and the reason is that it is the only component defined by a COST and a TYPE LINE rather than by an effect. The map groups on what the rest of the card says, so Blood Artist files with the drains, Indulgent Aristocrat with the sacrifice outlets, Charismatic Conqueror with the token makers, and the plain biters with the finishers. The leg that 95.1% of games open on has four addresses and no name. My ignition stage is deliberately narrower - the six members whose whole text is keywords, plus Edgar - which is a reading the map cannot express in either direction.

map_disagreements.component: wincon (this model's stage, not a declared component)
map_disagreements.why: The payload half of every checker-passed kill in this deck files in the city the map names for card draw. Bloodletter of Aclazotz, Sanctum Seeker, Bloodthirsty Conqueror and both loop halves (Vito, Sanguine Bond) sit in city-3 alongside Skullclamp, Night's Whisper, Champion of Dusk and Caretaker's Talent; only Edgar himself, who supplies four of stack 003's seven attackers, files elsewhere, in city-0 'Bodies'. The cause is sentence shape: 'whenever a creature dies, draw a card' and 'whenever a creature dies, each opponent loses 1 life' are the same clause with a different payload, and a cluster built from card text cannot separate refuel from kill. That collision is worth stating because it is also the deck's actual reading - the same deaths do both jobs - but a reader looking at the map will see a draw neighbourhood where the deck keeps its win.

map_disagreements.component: A free sacrifice outlet drawn (bloodline's new engine)
map_disagreements.why: Five of the thirteen scatter rows are fully coherent and this is the largest of them - seven cards, one city - yet the name the map gives that city is wrong for what these cards do here. The seven outlets cluster because Yahenni, Immersturm Predator and Mondrak all read as self-protection tricks - sacrifice to gain indestructible - so the map calls the region Insurance. In v1.0.1 they are the CONVERSION layer, and the card that makes them pay, Cordial Vampire, is filed two cities away in 'Finishers'. Agreement on membership, disagreement on job.

map_disagreements.component: A token multiplier or extra token-maker drawn
map_disagreements.why: The three doublers that stack 010 proves multiply together on one event have three different addresses: Anointed Procession and Elspeth, Storm Slayer in city-0, Mondrak in city-6 because its loud clause is the indestructible-counter activation, and Legion's Landing in city-4 'Ramp' because its back face is a land. A pilot reading the map would not learn that these are the same effect printed three times.

unassigned.why: A {1}{W} instant that puts +1/+1 counters on up to two creatures or proliferates. It touches the counters subtheme - Cordial Vampire, Indulgent Aristocrat, Vish Kal, Bloodflow Connoisseur, Mondrak's indestructible counter, Elspeth's loyalty - but no stage's job depends on it and it appears in no declared component, no verified pairing and no contained combo line. It is the one card in the 99 the engine model cannot give work to, and saying so is more useful than inventing a stage for it.

open_questions.question: With a free sacrifice outlet (Viscera Seer or Ashnod's Altar), Crossway Troublemakers AND High-Society Hunter on the battlefield, sacrifice N eminence tokens in one turn: how many cards are drawn, at what life cost, and does High-Society Hunter see ANY of them given its 'another nontoken creature' clause? Also: is a 1/1 black Vampire token 'a Vampire you control' for Crossway Troublemakers, and can the 2-life payment be declined per trigger?
open_questions.why_it_matters: This is the v1.0.1 engine in one board - the loop the pilot's 2026-09-01 game actually ran - and it is the only major stage-to-stage arrow in this model with no passing stack behind it. If High-Society Hunter is blind to tokens, the fuel stage is a card thinner than the declaration reads.

open_questions.question: Stack 002 records eminence tokens entering WITH Vampire Socialite's additional +1/+1 counter (an opponent had lost life earlier that turn); stack 011 records them entering WITHOUT it, because the only life loss that turn came from a trigger that had not yet resolved. What is the practical sequencing rule - does the pilot cast the Vampire before or after the turn's first drain, and does an attack-step Sanctum Seeker trigger resolving beat a post-combat cast?
open_questions.why_it_matters: It is a free two-power-per-token swing on the deck's most common turn, it is decided entirely by play order, and the two tracked stacks give opposite answers on boards that differ only in timing.

open_questions.question: Nothing measures whether a body is actually CONVERTED. The declaration prices 'a free sacrifice outlet drawn' at 77.6% and 'a drain that fires when a creature DIES' at 37.2% independently, but not the pair, and Forge cannot help: its evaluator activated Ashnod's Altar 0 times in 59 castings under both AI profiles and cast Viscera Seer 0 times in 500 games (both bench measurements on sacrifice decks, not taken on this list). Can the goldfish measure an outlet AND a death payoff together, and if not, what is the honest statement of what this stage's rate means?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The conversion stage is the whole of what v1.0.1 bought, and right now every figure attached to it measures a card being DRAWN. A stage nobody can measure is a stage the deck page will render as green.

open_questions.question: Both verified kill routes rest on a single card each (Bloodletter of Aclazotz 4.2% assembled, Bloodthirsty Conqueror 7.6%), and the deck holds exactly one tutor. Is a two-one-card-route wincon a correct shape for a bracket-4 aggro-ish list that now wins by attrition, or should the kill be an emergent property of the conversion layer with the two named cards demoted to bonuses?
open_questions.why_it_matters: It decides whether the next branch buys redundancy (more drain doublers, more tutors) or more conversion throughput, and the 400-game run already refuted the third option, which was more bodies.

proposed_goldfish_edits.change: Add High-Society Hunter to the component (currently 9 cards: Bloodtracker, Caretaker's Talent, Champion of Dusk, Crossway Troublemakers, Liliana Dreadhorde General, Night's Whisper, Preacher of the Schism, Skullclamp, Welcoming Vampire).
proposed_goldfish_edits.why: Its oracle text is 'Whenever another nontoken creature dies, draw a card' and card_roles.json already tags it draw:engine - it is the only card carrying that role that the component omits. The deck holds ten draw engines and the declaration measures nine, which understates the axis the pilot's four logged games identified as the deck's failure and which v1.0.1 was built to fix.

proposed_goldfish_edits.target: (new) A conversion pair online - an outlet AND a death payoff
proposed_goldfish_edits.change: Add an all_of target requiring one of {Altar of Dementia, Ashnod's Altar, Bloodflow Connoisseur, Immersturm Predator, Viscera Seer, Vish Kal Blood Arbiter, Yahenni Undying Partisan} AND one of {Blood Artist, Cruel Celebrant, Cordial Vampire, Crossway Troublemakers, Skullclamp, Liliana Dreadhorde General}.

Note the caveat in this deck's own history: an authored declaration is not evidence, so this target should be used to read a rate, never to split games for an engine-lift figure.

proposed_goldfish_edits.change: Rename to 'Protection held for the board' (membership unchanged: Teferi's Protection, Flawless Maneuver, Boros Charm, Akroma's Will, Deflecting Swat).

The same re-derivation that added the sacrifice-outlet target DELETED two swarm targets on the grounds that 400 Forge games refuted the go-wide thesis; this label is the last surviving reference to it, and a label is what a reader sees first.
